page.running_head: De Authoritate, & Dignitate Cap. I / SECT.XXVI. / Absurdè statui, Papam filios gignere tantùm per Vicarios.

main_text.p: toris ad plantatorem ; & super-edificatoris ad fundatorem. Hæc ille. Quæ ille quidem ab Hieronymo discere potuit, [Ego vos genui, ] id est, (inquit) r Hieron.in 1.Cor.4.{r}Me predicante vos in nouam vitam reformati estis. Omnes vero, qui ab alio geniti (nempe Pædagogi) ministrant, Patres dici non possunt. Proinde dum Tu Papam, quia gignit per Alios, fidelium Patrem esse contendis, ab exemplo Pauli, qui genuit per se, contra distertissimam Pauli sententiam: Patrem cum Pædagogo; Plantatorem cum Rigatore; Fundatorem cum Super-edificatore; Primum cum Secundo; Unum cum Alio perperam absurdeque confundis.
main_text.head: II. ANIMADVERSIO.
main_text.p: SPaulus prædicabat per se, & Fidelium Pater iure dici potuit: Papam autem prædicatorem ac Concionatorem per aliquot retrò secula vix sanè ullum historiæ vestræ meminerunt: ac propterea Tu, catus homo scilicet, eum Per alios gignentem introducis Patrem. Id quod nobis portenti simile videtur, uti & * Iam supra lib.r.* Hieronymo, qui aliorum Ministros Patres dici posse planè negat. Sed apud vos licet Confessariof Toletus lef. Instruct.Sacerd.lib.3. cap.11.§.Aducer-tendum 6.{c} Imponere pœnitentiam pœnitenti, per se, vel per alium implendam; ita ut unus pro alio ieiunet. Licet populo vestro in Sacramento{t} Spiritualiter comedere s Vincent. Serm. aftiu. in ofiauo corp.Christi.per Sacerdotem, tanquàm per os suum. Licet Papa spiritualiter gignere per alios. Denique vestra Affica[?] quid monstri non alit? De Pontificis officio prædicandi per se, & non per alium, pleniùs * differemus, cùm ad Pastoris Titulum discutiendum devenerimus.Simile habet Ecclesia in Enchirid. pag.114. Sacerdos in persona totius populi offert, & sumit sub utraque specie, in cuius persona totus populus spirituali quadam sumptione sanguinem Christi bibere gaudenter debet credere.* Infrà cap.2. §.16. & deinceps.

page.notes: The marginal note mark "r" is placed in the text before "Me predicante". The running head's title word "Authoritate" is read as "Autboritate" in the scan and may be a misreading; the chapter reference "Cap.I." is printed on the right of the running head. The scan is part 2 of a page, so the top shows only the running head. Doubtful readings: "Affica" (marked [?]; the A looks ornamented), "Iudæis" (marked [?]). The text marks {c} after Confessario and {t} after Sacramento have no matching visible note in the margin, and the note beginning "Simile habet" carries no mark. Margin notes are placed at the start of the paragraph or at approximate positions beside the lines, since their exact line positions are not certain. The final quotation keeps its printed quotation marks at the start of each line. The l in "lef." may be a misreading of "lib.".
